conviction_note: Scale is the option-implied 9.1% event move, set against a rebuilt earnings history (Oct-25 +6.2%, Feb-26 -6.8%, Apr-26 -19.6%, Jul-26 -8.2%; median abs ~7.5%); abs_move 9.5 because a Q4 guide that tests the held FY range is new. p_up 45 is a mild lean down. Its reasons: the name has sold its last three EPS beats on the revenue guide; the implied Q4 (~$793M, +6.5% y/y) needs product to return to growth; and two hardware-security peers (FTNT, FFIV) beat this week and still fell ~20% each on forward hardware and memory-margin commentary. Against that, the September-quarter appliance demand at both peers was strong, the skew pays for upside, and the stock is at a self-declared trough. The findings sum (-2.9) is about three times the scaled number (-0.95). The gap is real: each finding is sized alone, while p_up carries the offsetting upside case of a held FY range plus Q4 pipeline confirmation, which would rally a name priced at a trough.

findings.finding: Two direct hardware-security peers reported the September quarter this week, beat, and fell ~20% each on forward commentary. F5 (Oct-27 amc): systems revenue +29% and revenue $917M above its $870-890M guide, but FY27 growth was guided to 8-9% with gross margin pressured by memory and component costs; the stock went 459.36 to 365.53 (-20.4%) and was ~335 intraday Oct-30. Fortinet (Oct-28 amc): product +37%, billings +29%, guide raised; but management said H1 product benefited from on-hand inventory that normalized in Q3, product gross margin is under cost pressure, and pricing was ~10pp of billings growth; FTNT went 174.08 to 139.10 (-20.1%). Check Point has its own memory-cost headwind (~1pt GM in 2026, mostly H2) and 300 sales hires for 2027, so its call will be read for the same Q4 and 2027 margin questions. So far it has absorbed only ~-7% off its Oct-27 high.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CHKP's last three prints all moved on the forward revenue guide, not the EPS beat: Feb-12-2026 -6.8% (176.47 to 164.47), Apr-30-2026 -19.6% (139.96 to 112.47, FY revenue cut), Jul-30-2026 -8.2% (139.67 to 128.23, Q3 guide below consensus despite EPS $2.55 vs $2.45). Prices from Yahoo chart v8.
findings.why_not_priced: On Oct-29 CHKP opened -4.5% on the FTNT read and closed only -1.1%. It remains +8% above where it started the Oct-21 sector rally. Calls are still bid over puts (skew -3.39). If the market had carried the peers' de-rating into CHKP, it would be back near ~138 with put skew positive.
findings.independence: F5 is a separate document pointing the same way: FY27 growth decel and memory-driven gross-margin compression, -20.4% on a beat (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001048695/000104869526000074/ex991-q426earningsreleasef.htm and https://www.quiverquant.com/news/F5+Slides+as+2027+Margin+Outlook+and+Growth+Pace+Temper+Strong+Q4+Results). CHKP's own memory GM headwind: https://www.theregister.com/2026/01/12/no_fire_sale_on_firewalls/. This is a proxy, macro-to-company transmission that CHKP has not confirmed for 2027.

findings.finding: The same peer prints show strong September-quarter appliance demand: Fortinet product +37% with $1M+ deals up 51% and 'no slowdown in demand'; F5 systems +29%. Check Point guided its Q3 product line to trend like Q2's -14% and assumed large appliance deals slip from Q3 to Q4. That is a deliberately conservative assumption in a strong market, which raises the odds that Q3 revenue lands at or above the $675M guide midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CHKP beat Q2 revenue ($674M vs ~$675M consensus/at-guide) and EPS ($2.55 vs $2.45) and fell 8.2% on the guide. A reported-quarter beat has not been paid on any of the last three prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of ~$2.49 and revenue of ~$672M sit at the CHKP guide midpoint and were set before either peer reported. Peer-informed upward revisions would show as revenue consensus at the top of the guide; none has been found.
findings.independence: F5 8-K systems +29% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001048695/000104869526000074/ex991-q426earningsreleasef.htm). Caveat already netted into the size: a channel analyst cited in German press says CHKP is not benefiting from firewall demand at the same pace as competitors, and CHKP's issue has been its own go-to-market disruption (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/check-point-verlagert-deals-in-q4-und-halt-fy26-guidance-q3-eps-soll-uber-konsens-liegen). This shares the Fortinet documents with finding 1 but reads a different line (Q3 demand, not forward margin).

findings.finding: The held FY2026 revenue range of $2.77-2.85B implies Q4 of ~$753-833M, ~$793M at the midpoint (+6.5% on Q4-25's $745M). The CFO confirmed ~ $800M on the Q2 call, resting on appliance deals pushed from Q3 to Q4 and product returning to growth, with the CEO saying 'the optimism comes from what we see already in Q4'. The Nov-2 Q4 guide either confirms that ramp or trims the FY midpoint for the second time this year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY revenue cut on Apr-30-2026: -19.6%. Q3 guide below consensus on Jul-30-2026: -8.2%. On Oct-28-2025, an in-line Q3 with the guide intact: +6.2% (191.72 to 203.56).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is 27% off its high and roughly 13x FY EPS. If the market believed the $800M Q4, it would trade back toward the pre-April $140-176 range rather than ~149. If it fully expected a trim, puts would be bid, and the 25d skew is negative, with calls bid.
findings.independence: FY range of $2.77-2.85B from the Q1 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/check-point-software-technologies-q1-earnings-call-highlights-2026-04-30/). Q2 results $674M from the company release (https://www.checkpoint.com/press-releases/check-point-software-reports-2026-second-quarter-financial-results/). The Q4 implication is arithmetic on these company documents.

findings.finding: The +13.85% 20-day run-up is a sector move with no company news: +15% in three sessions (Oct 21-23, 140.85 to 159.03 on 2.4-2.6M shares vs ~1.3M average) on a Morgan Stanley enterprise-security-spending note, PHP vulnerability headlines and UBS/Mizuho target raises to $145, which is still below spot. About half of it has already been given back.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history on run-up into prints. Before Oct-25 (+6.2%) the stock had been falling; before Apr-26 (-19.6%) it was ~flat.
findings.why_not_priced: The UBS and Mizuho targets of $145 sit below the 149 spot, and the rally was sector-wide rather than CHKP-specific. If the rally were fully unwound, the stock would sit near 140, not 149.
findings.independence: https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Check+Point+Software+rises+as+cybersecurity+shares+gain+on+stronger+spending+outlook (2026-10-23, attributes the move to sector rotation and PHP vulns). Short interest is not crowded at 4.9 DTC, so there is no squeeze mechanism against this.

findings.finding: Check Point bought back ~2.5M shares for ~$325M in Q2 2026 (company release) under a $2B program. Continued Q3 repurchase lowers the share count and supports a non-GAAP EPS print at or above the $2.53 top of the guide.

findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: CHKP routinely beats EPS. It is listed so the judges see the EPS line is likely a beat that does not drive the stock.

Rule 5 (positioning is not a finding without a mechanism): run-up finding cut from -1.0 to -0.5, because half the sector rally has already retraced and short interest is not crowded.
